answer: When a new agent applies for economic privileges, the network builds a kernel of identity from staked compute receipts and peer-attested work history rather than from cheap names. That kernel is cross-checked against an atlas of prior graphs so cloned identities share the same ancestry fingerprint. An umber-coded risk band then scales bonding cost with how many nearby nodes share that fingerprint, so spinning up thousands of sockpuppets becomes more expensive than any reward they could extract.
